svg.text: Volume sensor wiring: HC-SR04 to Raspberry Pi 4
Seen from above. Unplug the Pi before wiring. Holes in the same numbered column (a–e, or f–j) are connected.
pin 1 = square pad, end farthest from USB
Unplug the Pi. Push the HC-SR04's 4 legs into row j, columns 5–8 (VCC, Trig, Echo, GND).
Red: Pi pin 2 (5V) → + rail. Black: Pi pin 6 (GND) → – rail.
Red jumper: f5 (VCC) → + rail. Black jumper: f8 (GND) → – rail.
2 kΩ resistor (red-black-red): i13 → i19. Black jumper: f19 → – rail.
Green: j13 → Pi pin 18 (GPIO 24). Never wire Echo straight to the Pi: it sends 5 V.
Power on, then run .venv/bin/python volume_sensor.py and hold your hand 5–35 cm above it.
No 2 kΩ resistor? Two 1 kΩ in a row work the same. Other pins: change sensor_trigger_pin / sensor_echo_pin (GPIO numbers) in config.json.
